newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia cenbank hopes BIS to help Yugo gold split.
newsitem.headline: Croatia cenbank hopes BIS to help Yugo gold split.

text.p: The National Bank of Croatia said on Tuesday it expected full membership of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) to help speed up a split of former Yugoslav assets among successor states.
Central banks of four new states -- Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Macedonia -- were invited to join the Swiss-based BIS earlier this month.
"The National Bank of Croatia will become a full member of the BIS at its annual meeting on June 9. This is a big achievement," governor Marko Skreb told reporters.
"Although our satisfaction is not complete, as it does not yet involve the division of gold and shares of former Yugoslavia, we hope to be able to push for it as members from inside (BIS)."

Skreb referred to an estimated $600 million in gold and cash of the now defunct National Bank of Yugoslavia, held at the BIS since before the country fell apart in 1991, and its 8,000 shares with suspended voting rights.
After staving off talks on division of these federal assets, the central bank of Yugoslavia, which now comprises Serbia and Montenegro, was not offered membership of the BIS.
Skreb said Croatia counted on the BIS's support in refinancing its debt in the case of balance of payments difficulties and also hoped to get access to all kinds of financial information.
